bug_description.normalized: The PhaseOneDecompressor fuzzer lets attacker-controlled input define image dimensions and strip descriptors. The vulnerable constructor only checks that the number of strips equals image height; it does not verify that strip row numbers are unique and cover every row. The staged 48-byte witness builds a 2x3 U16 image and three zero-length strips all targeting row 0. Decompression therefore writes row 0 three times and leaves rows 1 and 2 in the newly allocated image buffer untouched. RawImageData::checkMemIsInitialized then asks MemorySanitizer to verify every row, and the check on an untouched 4-byte row reports use-of-uninitialized-value.

source.code: const rawspeed::uint32 width = bs->getU32(); const rawspeed::uint32 height = bs->getU32(); const rawspeed::uint32 type = bs->getU32(); const rawspeed::uint32 cpp = bs->getU32();
source.description: First project-code read of the attacker buffer on the vulnerable path: the fuzzer header fields that determine image dimensions and the decompressor preconditions are parsed from the witness bytes.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_10841/poc` begins with little-endian u32 values `width=2`, `height=3`, `type=TYPE_USHORT16 (0)`, and `cpp=1`; those exact values are later materialized into `mRaw` and allow the malformed strip table to reach decompression.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.code: const auto numStrips = bs.getU32(); std::generate_n(std::back_inserter(strips), numStrips, [&bs]() -> rawspeed::PhaseOneStrip { const int n = bs.getU32(); const auto stripLen = bs.getU32(); return {n, bs.getStream(stripLen)}; });
tainted_value_origin.description: This read block materializes the vulnerability-critical strip table from the remaining attacker bytes. In the witness, `numStrips=3` and each generated `PhaseOneStrip` has `n=0` and `stripLen=0`, so the table has the correct length but names only row 0.

sink.description: MSAN sink. The row checker passes one image row and its 4-byte logical row size into `MSan::CheckMemIsInitialized`; when that row was never written by decompression, the sanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value.
sink.note: The staged MSAN trace reports uninitialized bytes at offset 0 inside a 4-byte region and shows this call beneath `RawImageData::checkMemIsInitialized()`.

root_cause.description: The constructor validates only strip count. A strip table whose length matches the image height is accepted even if the per-strip row numbers are duplicated and do not cover every row.
root_cause.note: For the witness, `strips.size()==3` and `mRaw->dim.y==3`, so this check passes even though every `PhaseOneStrip::n` is 0. The staged patch fixes the bug by adding `validateStrips()` to reject duplicate or out-of-range row numbers before decompression.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness header also satisfies the earlier constructor guards (`type == TYPE_USHORT16`, `cpp == 1`, `bpp == 2`, `width == 2`, `height == 3`), and this size check evaluates false because `numStrips == height == 3`. The malformed duplicate-row strip table is therefore admitted into the decompressor.

fine_trace.code: const rawspeed::uint32 width = bs->getU32(); const rawspeed::uint32 height = bs->getU32(); const rawspeed::uint32 type = bs->getU32(); const rawspeed::uint32 cpp = bs->getU32();
fine_trace.note: Reads the attacker-controlled image header fields. The witness sets `width=2`, `height=3`, `type=TYPE_USHORT16`, and `cpp=1`, establishing the small three-row U16 image that passes the decompressor's basic preconditions.

fine_trace.code: rawspeed::RawImage mRaw(rawspeed::RawImage::create(rawspeed::RawImageType(type))); mRaw->dim = rawspeed::iPoint2D(width, height); mRaw->setCpp(cpp); mRaw->isCFA = isCFA;
fine_trace.note: Materializes the parsed header into the `RawImage`: the object now represents a `2x3` U16 image, so later code allocates three rows, expects three strips, and checks three rows for initialization.

fine_trace.code: const auto numStrips = bs.getU32(); std::generate_n(std::back_inserter(strips), numStrips, [&bs]() -> rawspeed::PhaseOneStrip { const int n = bs.getU32(); const auto stripLen = bs.getU32(); return {n, bs.getStream(stripLen)}; });
fine_trace.note: Reads the strip table from the remaining attacker bytes. The witness sets `numStrips=3`, then creates three `PhaseOneStrip` entries with `n=0` and `stripLen=0`, so the table has the right length but covers only row 0.

The only strip admission check compares vector length to image height. Because both are 3 for the witness, the constructor accepts the malformed strip table even though step 3 provided no strip for rows 1 or 2.

Allocates the raw image buffer for the three-row image. This heap storage starts uninitialized, and the staged MSAN trace identifies this allocation chain as the origin of the poisoned bytes later observed at the sink.

fine_trace.code: for (size_t i = t->start; i < t->end && i < strips.size(); i++) decompressStrip(strips[i]);
fine_trace.note: The decompressor forwards each accepted strip to `decompressStrip`. Since every `strips[i].n` from step 3 is 0, every iteration operates on another row-0 strip and no iteration ever targets row 1 or row 2.

This row-pointer derivation turns each forwarded strip into a concrete destination row. With the witness `strip.n==0` every time, `getData(0, strip.n)` always aliases row 0, so rows 1 and 2 are never selected for writing.

For the witness width 2, the loop stays on the `getBits(16)` path for both pixels. The zero-length strip buffers from step 3 do not abort here because `BitStream::fillSafe` zero-pads exhausted input, so these duplicate strips still write defined zeros into row 0 while rows 1 and 2 remain untouched from step 5.

fine_trace.code: for (int j = 0; j < uncropped_dim.y; j++) checkRowIsInitialized(j);
fine_trace.note: After decompression, the MSAN-only verifier walks every row of the uncropped image. Because steps 6-8 only ever selected and wrote row 0, this loop eventually invokes `checkRowIsInitialized` on an untouched row buffer.

Sink. `rowsize` is `bpp * uncropped_dim.x = 4` bytes for the two-pixel U16 row. When `curr_line` points to one of the untouched rows reached by step 9, `MSan::CheckMemIsInitialized` reports uninitialized bytes at offset 0 of that 4-byte region.

allocation_stack.function: unsigned char* rawspeed::alignedMallocArray<unsigned char, 16ul, false>(unsigned long, unsigned long)

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context identifies the heap buffer whose bytes remain poisoned; the actual bug is the earlier acceptance of duplicate row metadata that leaves part of that allocation unwritten.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds `PhaseOneDecompressor::validateStrips()` and calls it from the constructor. That new validation rejects duplicate or out-of-range `strip.n` values before `createData()` and `decompress()` can leave rows unwritten, so it addresses the witnessed duplicate-row strip table.

poc.trigger: A 48-byte little-endian fuzzer input that encodes a `2x3` U16 image and three zero-length strips all with row index `n=0`.

format.name: PhaseOneDecompressorFuzzer little-endian struct
format.contract: Exact staged witness layout: `width=2`, `height=3`, `type=TYPE_USHORT16 (0)`, `cpp=1`, `isCFA=0x20202020`, `numStrips=3`, followed by three strip records `{n=0, stripLen=0}` and no strip payload bytes. The trigger relies on `numStrips == height` so the constructor's size-only check passes while duplicate row-0 strip descriptors leave rows 1 and 2 unwritten.
